data.gender_notes: Isidor is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In ancient Greek mythology, the name Isidor comes from the combination of Isis, the goddess of fertility, and doron, meaning 'gift'. It was believed that children given this name were protected by the goddess Isis and would receive her blessings. The name Isidor carries the meaning “Gifted by Isis” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Isidor usually hope their child will grow to embody gifted by isis and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Ισίδωρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ισίδωρος προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'Ισις' που σημαίνει Θεός και 'δωρος' που σημαίνει δώρο. Ο Ισίδωρος ήταν ένα κοινό όνομα μεταξύ των πρώτων Χριστιανών και συνδέεται στενά με τον Άγιο Ισίδωρο της Σεβίλλης, ο οποίος ήταν εξέχων θεολόγος και ερμηνευτής των Γραφών.
